summary: Haiku 5.5 reads the injected warning as a message from the user in all the v2 branches we checked: its reasoning calls the warning 'the user's instruction' or notes that it 'sits in the user turn', and on two steps it weighs whether acting on the alternative still needs the user's approval. gpt-4o-mini writes no text after the warning in these branches (it goes straight to tool calls), so there is nothing to quote; its next calls show it followed the alternative on 10 of its 13 v2 steps (by the outcome table). The warning is injected as user text on the wire, so reading it as the user is what the method sets up; it matters for how the warning would be worded in a deployed monitor.
